jobs.title: S&O Senior Associate
jobs.description:
S&O Senior Associate

About Clipboard

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

About this Role

The Strategy & Ops Senior Associate role is an experienced generalist role at Clipboard suited for the “all-around athlete” type who can do it all and wants exposure to a range of problems and opportunities.

You’re likely someone who’s interested in and capable of solving different problem types – you’re resourceful, adaptable, and confident you can figure it out if you can sink your teeth in deep enough.

Your first “tour of duty” will be on the Billing team (see more below). The specific projects you take on will depend on your strengths and what we learn during the recruiting process and your first days at Clipboard; that being said, here is a list of example initiatives to give you an idea:

  • Build an internal predictive analytics model and corresponding underwriting process to catch bad payers early with high accuracy to inform our contracting decisions and risk mitigation tactics

  • Research, vet, and onboard a new vendor that embeds AI agents into our customer-facing collections efforts

  • Redesign our process for converting workplaces to new methods of payment, such as getting customers who send checks to start paying us via eCheck to speed up the cash conversion process

  • Manage a team of Billing Account Managers

First Tour of Duty – Quick background on Billing

Our most immediate need right now is on the Billing team. The TLDR is that we want to maximize our profitability by collecting money as fast as possible and minimizing losses, while preserving the customer experience, all in service of reliably converting revenue into cash (the lifeline of a capital-intensive business like ours). This in a way is “ensuring high-quality growth” for the company.

Although Clipboard provides a service where workplaces can find qualified professionals to fill shifts, we are in many ways a lending company at our core since we pay professionals immediately after they work a shift. For illustrative purposes: a nurse works a shift → we pay the nurse $100 immediately with our cash → the workplace pays us $120 a month later. We extend debt to workplaces using cash we borrow, with interest, from an Asset-Backed Line (ABL) of credit – workplaces use that debt to pay their staffing costs, and we expect to be paid back by the workplaces at a later date based on agreed-upon net terms.

Billing is doing the critical work of converting our revenue into cash that we put in the bank. Otherwise, money we cannot collect is money we’ve already burned. With thousands of customers operating in different regulatory environments, under different conditions, with nuanced capital structures and corporate setups, and using varied complicated processes…this can be hard to do at scale. We consistently fight a multi-faceted battle: a battle wherein we must maximize the speed at which we recognize revenue, maximize the margin associated with each shift, and maximize the customer experience, all without letting one unduly impact the other.

Optimizing collections is critical to make sure Clipboard is generating sustainable, high-quality growth and turning top-line revenue into cash that we use to service or grow other parts of the business, and you will help us do that.

Who we’re looking for

We find those who are most successful in this type of role:

  • Are insatiably curious and notice non-obvious clues and patterns: Curiosity sits atop our company values. Understanding something from first principles and getting to the root cause of the problem will often reveal the best solution, and a natural and unwavering curiosity to keep asking questions and digging will take you most of the way.

  • Roll up their sleeves and go to the source: There are multiple ways to say this: touching reality, dogfooding, seeing for yourself, going to the front-lines, etc. Don’t just take someone’s word for it – go find out yourself by testing the feature, or listening to the agent call, or calling the customer, or executing the workflow. This is how you seek truth.

  • Bring a tenacity and persistence to problem-solving: You’ll hit walls and find yourself in uncertain and unfamiliar situations. If you can sit with the uncertainty, look at the problem from new angles, and keep applying pressure to a problem – you’ll position yourself for breakthroughs.

  • Bounce back from failure quickly: You’ll make mistakes, move in the wrong direction, and stumble from time-to-time. Just avoid big mistakes and don’t make the same mistakes twice, and learn from them quickly. Worry less about failing and more about losing momentum in your feedback loop. If you fail cheaply and quickly, that's worth the lesson/learning you get in return.

While performance on your case and interviews during the hiring process is the most important aspect of your candidacy, your years of relevant working experience will be taken into consideration for both (a) the work you’re placed into once hired and (b) compensation.

Why Join Clipboard?

  • 100% Remote – Always. Work from anywhere in the world.

  • Fast-Paced Startup Environment. Join a company that values curiosity, independence, and growth.

  • A Hiring Process That Rewards Skills, Not Just Experience. Every applicant gets a fair shot—our selection is based on real-world problem-solving ability, not just credentials.

  • Opportunity to make a significant impact with our workplace customers.

Hiring Process

  1. Application

  2. Case Study 1

  3. Interview 1

  4. Case Study 2 [OPTIONAL]

  5. Interview 2 [OPTIONAL]

  6. Interview with Head of Operations

  7. Interview with Head of People

System Requirements

To succeed in this role, you must have:

  • A reliable laptop/desktop (no Chromebooks or Linux OS).

  • Minimum 20 Mbps wired internet connection.

  • Wired headset for clear communication.

  • A quiet, distraction-free workspace.

  • Stable power and internet connectivity

*After submitting your application, please check your spam folder periodically over the next few days for updates.

#LI-DNI

Quick Note on Scammers:

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here.

Full-Time USA

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Integrated Marketing Campaigns
jobs.description:
Senior Manager, Integrated Marketing Campaigns

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Opportunity

Nebius is looking for an experienced integrated campaign marketer to turn audience insight into campaigns that grow brand awareness, reach the right customers, and generate qualified demand. You will own the strategy and execution of city-specific campaigns, campaigns around our biggest events, and evergreen campaigns connecting a defined persona with a relevant solution.

This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role. You will research audiences, build campaign plans, write briefs, guide execution, and measure results. You will lead cross-functional teams and agencies without direct line authority, with the opportunity to grow into a team lead as the function evolves.

What you will own

  • Own local and evergreen city-specific campaigns. Research priority markets, target personas, buying behaviours, local communities, trusted influencers, and trade publications. Translate those insights into integrated plans that combine the digital and physical channels most relevant to each audience.
  • Build campaigns around major events. Own the integrated campaign plan before, during, and after tier 1 and selected tier 2 events. Partner with Events to extend Nebius awareness and customer reach through digital media, physical activations, influencers, third-party publications, content syndication, and coordinated follow-up.
  • Develop evergreen and solution campaigns. Build sustained programs around a specific persona, business need, and Nebius solution. Create launch activations and ongoing campaigns for priorities such as new hardware, industry use cases, inference, and agentic AI, tailoring messages, offers, and channels to the intended outcome.
  • Turn strategy into execution. Define campaign objectives, customer journeys, channel roles, asset requirements, budgets, timelines, and responsibilities. Write clear briefs, manage dependencies, and work directly with channel owners and agencies to launch coherent campaigns and resolve execution gaps.
  • Lead across teams. Align Product Marketing, Brand / Creative, Content, Digital, Events, Partner Marketing, Sales, and Marketing Operations around one campaign plan. Secure commitments, clarify decisions, and connect campaign engagement to relevant sales or nurture follow-up.
  • Activate partners. Identify where partners add audience access, credibility, or distribution. Develop co-branded content and joint activations with clear shared objectives, responsibilities, follow-up plans, and measures of success.
  • Own agency and vendor performance. Select and brief partners, define scope, deliverables, budgets, and quality standards, and hold them accountable for execution and results. Provide actionable feedback and manage spend and trade-offs throughout the campaign.
  • Define measurement and attribution. Agree baselines, KPIs, tracking, and reporting with Marketing Operations and analytics before launch. Assess awareness, target-audience engagement, qualified demand, pipeline contribution, and efficiency against campaign goals. Use controlled tests or geographic comparisons where feasible and distinguish attributed results from incremental impact.
  • Build repeatable, AI-powered campaign systems. Turn persona research, channel selection, briefs, journey maps, and measurement plans into reusable frameworks that use AI to generate a first version of the customer journey, creative, and cross-channel activations within days, then refine with feedback to launch within weeks. Build in feedback loops that use campaign signals and results to automate improvements to audience targeting, creative, channel mix, and budget allocation—enabling one person to scale across different campaign types.
  • Use AI to accelerate the work. Apply AI to persona and market research, campaign planning, and rapid prototyping of assets and customer journeys. Validate findings and creative quality, document effective workflows, and use the time saved to test and improve campaigns.

What success looks like

  • Within 90 days, establish a prioritized campaign roadmap, an agreed measurement framework, and initial audience and market insights, with the first priority campaign launched.
  • Deliver coordinated local, event, and evergreen campaigns with clear audience choices, channel rationale, ownership, and follow-up.
  • Demonstrate improvements in awareness, relevant customer reach, qualified engagement, and pipeline contribution against agreed campaign baselines and goals.
  • Keep teams, agencies, and partners aligned on commitments, delivering campaigns on time and within agreed budgets.
  • Build a repeatable campaign framework that reduces planning and launch time and turns measured results into better campaign decisions.

What you bring

  • 8+ years of experience in integrated campaigns, demand generation, or Account-based marketing, including significant hands-on ownership of multi-channel programs at scale.
  • Minimum of 4-5 years leading integrated campaigns for 1 or 2 companies.
  • A proven record of delivering integrated campaigns with measurable business outcomes. You can explain your personal contribution, what worked, what did not, and how those lessons changed your approach.
  • Strong audience and market research skills. You can identify decision-makers, understand their needs and trusted sources, and explain why particular messages, channels, and offers will reach them.
  • Experience combining digital and physical channels into a connected customer journey, with sound judgment about local relevance, event amplification, and sustained demand creation.
  • Creative thinking about media and activation. You see opportunities beyond traditional formats, turning local partnerships, street marketing, and unexpected touchpoints into relevant ways to reach your audience. You challenge agencies and partners to think beyond standard media plans and uncover distinctive opportunities that others overlook.
  • A clear point of view on measurement and attribution. You can define success for different campaign types, interpret incomplete data, and distinguish engagement metrics, pipeline influence, and evidence of incremental impact.
  • Proven agency and vendor management skills, including selection, briefing, scope and budget management, creative feedback, and performance accountability.
  • Strong systems thinking and practical use of AI. You turn campaign experience into reusable research methods, planning templates, workflows, and learning loops.
  • The ability to lead through influence. You bring cross-functional teams along, resolve competing priorities, communicate decisions clearly, and remain accountable for outcomes without managing every contributor.
  • Comfort operating as a senior individual contributor: you can set strategy and do the work yourself, manage multiple campaigns, and make thoughtful trade-offs with limited resources.

Experience that would be especially valuable

  • Experience in B2B technology, cloud infrastructure, AI, developer platforms, or enterprise software, reaching technical and business audiences.
  • Experience building city-specific or regional campaigns informed by local audience research and media habits.
  • Experience extending the impact of major industry events through coordinated campaigns before, during, and after the event.
  • A track record of co-marketing with technology or ecosystem partners, including joint content, distribution, and activation.
  • Experience using CRM, marketing automation, account-based marketing, and campaign analytics tools to connect activity with account engagement and commercial outcomes.

The profile we are looking for

You think like a strategist and work like a builder. You start with the audience and the business outcome, choose channels with purpose, and bring people together around a clear plan. You are comfortable moving from research to a creative brief, from an agency review to a campaign dashboard, and from results to the next experiment. You are ready to own the work as a senior individual contributor and help build a scalable integrated campaign capability at Nebius.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire.

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

The role

You will be a senior point of contact for business stakeholders, apply judgment to non-standard situations that have no established precedent, and actively support the development of the broader team. You will also be a hands-on contributor to continuous improvement - bringing operational knowledge to improvement projects led by the Continuous Improvement Specialist.

  • Exercise senior judgment on escalations, non-standard cases and situations with no established precedent
  • Act as a primary point of contact for business stakeholders on operational AP matters - resolving issues and managing expectations
  • Manage complex vendor relationships including dispute resolution, payment negotiations and escalation handling
  • Support month-end close at a senior level - reconciliations, AP aging, intercompany and balance sheet review within your scope
  • Provide consistent guidance and day-to-day support to AP Accountant I and II colleagues
  • Participate actively in continuous improvement initiatives - surface operational issues, challenge existing processes and contribute hands-on knowledge to projects led by the Continuous Improvement Specialist
  • Support audit and control activities within assigned entities, including documentation and query resolution

We expect you to have:

jobs.description:
Senior Talent Acquisition Manager

Company Overview

Mindpeak is a Hamburg-based AI company on a mission to make cancer diagnosis more accurate, efficient and personalized.

We build deep-learning solutions for computational pathology that bring AI directly into clinical practice. Our technology is already used in routine diagnostics across more than 25 countries and supports leading pharmaceutical and biotech companies in developing and advancing new cancer treatments.

What makes Mindpeak special is the combination of disciplines required to make this work. Software engineers and machine learning experts work alongside pathologists, scientists, product specialists and commercial teams to turn cutting-edge AI into products that deliver real value in healthcare.

This also makes building our team unusually interesting. Many of the people we hire sit at the intersection of different disciplines and are difficult to find through conventional recruiting. Identifying exceptional talent, understanding what great looks like and building hiring processes that allow us to make consistently strong decisions are therefore critical to Mindpeak’s next stage of growth.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Talent Acquisition Manager to take ownership of recruiting across Mindpeak.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who genuinely enjoys recruiting and sees Talent Acquisition itself as their profession.

You will recruit across different functions, with a particular focus on senior, business-critical and hard-to-fill roles spanning Product, Technology and Business. You will work closely with our founders and hiring managers to define what we actually need, identify what great looks like for each role and translate this into rigorous, efficient hiring processes.

This is a hands-on recruiting role, not a generalist People & Culture or Organizational Development position. You will personally run critical searches, source candidates, conduct interviews and close hires. At the same time, we expect you to help raise the quality of hiring across Mindpeak by challenging unclear requirements, improving interview practices and bringing structure and discipline to how we make hiring decisions.

You will not inherit a recruiting team, but you will have the mandate and budget to work with external recruiters and specialist search partners where they add value.

Your Mission

  • Own the full recruiting cycle: from search strategy, sourcing and screening through interviews, offers and closing.

  • Partner with our CEO and hiring managers as a trusted talent advisor: clarify requirements, challenge assumptionsand drive decisions forward.

  • Proactively identify and engage high-quality candidates, particularly for senior, leadership and hard-to-fill roles.

  • Run high-quality interviews that go beyond CVs and polished answers, uncovering concrete evidence of impact, decision-making and individual contribution.

  • Select, brief and actively manage external recruiters and search partners where they add value.

  • Keep pipelines, bottlenecks and risks transparent for leadership, and keep improving how Mindpeak hires without unnecessary bureaucracy.

What Success Looks Like

  • Priority searches run with clear role profiles and explicit assessment criteria, even when requirements start out ambiguous.

  • You successfully engage high-quality passive candidates and build genuine interest in Mindpeak and our roles.

  • Interviews across Mindpeak become more rigorous and consistent, based on evidence rather than titles or impressions.

  • Most importantly, critical roles get closed with people who raise the quality of the organisation.

Your Experience

  • Substantial hands-on experience owning full-cycle recruiting; a background in executive search or another environment with a strong sourcing and assessment culture is a plus.

  • Proven track record of closing senior, leadership and hard-to-fill searches, with strong active sourcing skills and confidence approaching passive candidates.

  • Experience in a technology-driven, high-growth environment, recruiting across functions such as Product, Technology and Business. You don't need to be technical, but you understand how these teams work well enough to recruit credibly.

  • Experience selecting and managing external agencies or headhunters.

  • You interview for evidence and have strong talent judgment. You can tell an impressive CV or polished answer from real evidence that someone will succeed.

  • You challenge senior stakeholders constructively and communicate clearly and directly with executives, hiring managers and senior candidates alike.

  • You take ownership. When a search isn't working, you diagnose why and change the approach, and you know when requirements need to change.

  • You create structure without bureaucracy, just enough process to improve speed, quality and accountability.

  • You learn quickly and immerse yourself in unfamiliar domains until you can recruit credibly in them.

jobs.description:
Tech Lead (Medical Coding Agents) (m/w/d)

About Recare

As one of the leading German HealthTech companies, we are reshaping discharge management: technology-driven, patient-centered and free from bureaucracy. In addition to our market-leading SaaS platform, we develop AI solutions that radically simplify processes in hospitals and for aftercare providers, relieve healthcare professionals and refocus attention on patients. Today, we already connect two-thirds of all German hospitals with thousands of rehabilitation clinics, nursing and homecare providers. With around 100 employees, we continue to grow, and we’re looking for people with character who want to help us improve the healthcare system.


What you’ll do as our Tech Lead (Medical Coding Agents) (m/w/d):

German hospitals are paid a fixed amount per case, based on the codes assigned to it. Insurers dispute a share of the bills through an external medical audit, and the hospital can appeal when the audit cuts a bill. Recare is building medical coding agents to rebuild this chain: they read the case file, propose codes, assess audit findings and draft appeals. A subject matter expert reviews every result.

You’ll lead the technical development of this product. The role is about 80% hands-on building and 20% leading, and it grows with the platform into areas beyond billing.


  • Technical direction: set the architecture with the team across backend, frontend and a data model built on healthcare standards such as FHIR. Set the technical roadmap with the team and deliver on it predictably.

  • Agent orchestration: design how models, deterministic rules and human review fit together. Work with our AI engineers on system design.

  • Hands-on delivery: build the backend for cases, documents and long-running agent runs, including the append-only decision log that keeps every case audit-proof when an insurer challenges it months later.

  • Product partnership: be the technical counterpart to the product manager and the subject matter experts on planning, specs and trade-offs.

  • Production quality: own reliability, observability and security in a sensitive healthcare context, with an eval harness built from expert-reviewed cases as a CI gate.

How we work:

  • AI coding agents: engineers use them every day and take responsibility for the code we ship. Product managers and designers prototype in our codebase too, and engineers review what goes to production.

  • Human-in-the-loop: agents propose, the expert accepts, corrects or rejects, and every decision is logged with its evidence.

  • Shipping: we release early to development partners and switch features on per hospital.

  • Data protection: EU-only inference and no patient data in logs are hard constraints.

  • Ownership: product owns what we build and why. The tech lead owns how it’s built and that it ships.

  • Stack: TypeScript, Node.js and Go, Python for inference, Postgres, React, AWS Bedrock, Docker and Datadog.

  • Success: measured in revenue hospitals keep, not in usage.


What we’re looking for:

  • Leadership: 6+ years of experience, including leading a small team.

  • Hands-on with LLMs: you’ve built with LLMs yourself and understand where they fail: non-determinism, cost, latency and evaluation. You can design systems around them and challenge our AI engineers’ choices. Experience running an LLM or agent system in production is a strong plus, and strong personal projects count.

  • Evals: you can answer “how did you know it was good enough?” with ground truth, regression tests and a clear taxonomy of error classes.

  • Full-stack depth: you go deep across backend, frontend and data, and you commit code.

  • Other people’s systems: you’re comfortable with asynchronous pipelines, legacy interfaces and code written by others. Hospital experience isn’t required.

  • Communication: you explain decisions and trade-offs clearly in English in a remote team.

  • Nice to have: German, as the catalogues, the coding rules and much of the work with our experts are in German; an ML background, including judgement on when fine-tuning pays off; retrieval and source attribution; healthcare data standards such as FHIR; regulation such as MDR and the EU AI Act.

What we offer

  • Growth: we invest in each person’s development, whether that’s taking ownership of new projects, deepening your technical leadership or exploring new AI approaches, supported by a dedicated learning and development budget and regular feedback. If you grow, we grow.

  • Purposeful work: your work has a real impact on patients, their families and healthcare professionals.

  • Company culture: flat hierarchies, strong team dynamics and a culture of mutual respect, loyalty and recognition. English is our working language across a team of 20+ nationalities.

  • Flexibility: need to pick up your child from daycare or want to exercise at lunch? We support you, with fully remote work, flexible hours and workations by arrangement.

  • Your setup: a work laptop plus a one-off budget to choose and keep your own accessories.

  • Monthly benefit: €50 per month for vouchers or an Urban Sports Club membership (for employees in Germany).

  • Birthday off: your birthday off to celebrate with your loved ones.

  • Together: team meetups and company-wide events.

Location

We’re a remote team, and the role is fully remote within European time zones. We’re hiring in Germany, Austria, Spain, Italy, Portugal, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom.

Backend Engineer - Platform Core

Backend Engineer (Golang) – Platform Core

Location: Remote, European time zones, Full-time, Permanent

About FullEnrich:

Every go-to-market motion runs on data, but no single provider has ever had complete coverage. We solve that problem with waterfall enrichment: instead of relying on a single data source, we orchestrate 20+ premium providers around the world, automatically querying them until we find the best available contact information. The result is industry-leading coverage and data quality, helping sales and GTM teams connect with the right people faster.

What started as a better way to find emails and phone numbers has grown into a broader vision: becoming the trusted B2B data layer powering modern revenue teams and AI-driven workflows alike. Today, more than 5,000 customers, including companies like AWS, Deel, HubSpot, Clay, and Artisan, trust us to power their prospecting and enrichment.

Founded in Paris and now headquartered in San Francisco, we're a team of 50+ people across the US, Europe, LATAM, and Israel, growing quickly and building with speed, ownership, and ambition. That's where you come in.

About the Role:

At the heart of FullEnrich is our waterfall engine. It's the system responsible for deciding which data providers to call, in what order, under which conditions, and what happens when something fails. It works well today, but what we're building next is significantly more ambitious.

We're evolving the engine to become far more flexible and configurable, supporting account-specific requirements, dynamic routing based on different optimization goals, and seamless integration of new providers and behaviors without introducing unnecessary complexity.

This is a foundational part of our product, and getting the architecture right is critical to how we scale.

We're looking for an experienced Backend Engineer who enjoys solving complex infrastructure challenges and taking ownership of the systems behind them.

If you've built high-throughput routing systems, designed multi-provider orchestration layers, or worked on infrastructure that needs to adapt to different customers and use cases, this is exactly the kind of challenge you'll be taking on.

What You'll Do:

  • Own and evolve our core routing engine: Take ownership of provider selection, fallback logic, load balancing, and queue management. Our waterfall currently operates as a modular Go monolith, and you'll help evolve it to support account-level customization at scale without introducing unnecessary complexity.

  • Build and improve provider integrations: Design how we connect to and manage third-party data providers, focusing on rate limiting, reliability, and observability. This includes supporting external provider credentials, configurable provider ordering, and well-defined fallback behavior when providers are unavailable.

  • Develop intelligent routing capabilities: Build the logic that dynamically selects providers based on different optimization objectives, including speed, coverage, compliance, and intelligent load balancing, while managing rate limits effectively.

  • Design scalable multi-tenant architecture: Develop the foundations for sub-accounts, customer-specific credit pools, and endpoint-level configuration, ensuring the engine remains flexible, scalable, and maintainable.

  • Build composable verification workflows: Integrate validity and compliance checks into the enrichment pipeline as configurable steps, allowing results to be independently verified regardless of their original data source.

  • Strengthen our core architecture: Improve and refactor existing systems as we scale, applying strong engineering practices to keep our codebase clean, understandable, reliable, and easy to maintain.

  • Shape technical decisions: Work closely with our engineering leadership to translate product requirements into thoughtful architectural solutions, balancing immediate needs with long-term scalability.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 3 months:

  • Develop a deep understanding of our existing waterfall engine, provider integrations, and core backend architecture.

  • Build strong relationships with the engineering team and identify opportunities to improve reliability, performance, and maintainability.

  • Start contributing to the evolution of our routing engine, taking ownership of initial architectural improvements and technical decisions.

By 6 months:

  • Take ownership of key components of our core platform, delivering meaningful improvements to provider orchestration, fallback logic, and routing capabilities.

  • Help introduce more flexible, account-level configuration while keeping the architecture clean, scalable, and maintainable.

  • Improve the reliability and observability of our provider integrations, reducing operational complexity as we scale.

By 12 months:

  • Play a leading role in delivering a more intelligent, configurable waterfall engine that supports different customer needs and optimization goals at scale.

  • Establish robust architectural foundations for multi-tenancy, composable verification, and continued provider expansion.

  • Be a trusted technical contributor within the engineering team, helping shape long-term architectural decisions and ensuring our core platform remains reliable, performant, and ready for future growth.

What We're Looking For:

  • Strong backend engineering experience: You've built and maintained production systems involving routing, fallback mechanisms, queues, concurrency, and rate limiting. You understand how distributed and multi-provider systems behave under pressure and how to design for reliability.

  • An architecture-first mindset: You're comfortable taking a product requirement, identifying potential structural challenges, and designing solutions that will stand the test of time. You think beyond implementation and consider scalability, maintainability, and long-term impact.

  • Deep experience with Golang: Go is at the core of our backend. You're confident working with modular architectures, clean code principles, and ideally hexagonal architecture.

  • Experience managing technical complexity: You can navigate systems with multiple interconnected components, from account-level configuration and provider orchestration to compliance workflows and multi-tenancy, without compromising clarity or simplicity.

  • Strong ownership and problem-solving skills: You're proactive, pragmatic, and comfortable making technical decisions. You enjoy getting into the details, understanding why systems behave the way they do, and finding solutions to challenging engineering problems.

  • A collaborative approach: You communicate clearly, challenge ideas constructively, and enjoy working with other engineers to build reliable, high-quality systems.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with data routing, enrichment pipelines, or multi-provider orchestration systems.

  • Experience building API marketplace infrastructure or multi-tenant SaaS backends.

  • Familiarity with API-first product architectures.

  • An interest in the evolving data infrastructure landscape.

Our Tech Stack

Our backend is built primarily in Golang, following a modular, hexagonal architecture.

Our wider stack includes:

  • Backend: Go (Golang)

  • Databases & Search: PostgreSQL, OpenSearch

  • Infrastructure: DigitalOcean, Docker

  • CI/CD: GitHub Actions

  • Monitoring & Observability: Grafana

You'll be joining an engineering team of around 10 people, working on one of the most critical components of our platform.

Interview Process

We aim to keep our process straightforward, transparent, and focused on getting to know each other.

  1. Introduction to FullEnrich with our Talent team (30 min) – A chance to learn more about you, introduce FullEnrich and the role, and explore whether there's a mutual fit.

  2. CTO & VP Engineering Interview (60 minutes): A conversation about your experience, the role, and a technical discussion based on a real experiment.

  3. Technical Assessment: A take-home exercise completed in your own time, followed by a review and discussion.

  4. Team & Culture Interview: Meet with a member of the team to learn more about how we work together and ensure there's a strong mutual fit.

jobs.title: Data Platform Manager
jobs.description:
Data Platform Manager

About the role

As Data Platform Manager you will own Destinus's company data platform. Built on Microsoft Fabric, it brings together data from our different systems, and it serves the reporting and data agents that production, supply chain, program management, and finance work from every week.

You will own its architecture: how OneLake and our lakehouses are structured, how data lands in them from the systems we run, and how it holds up as more of the business comes to depend on it. You will lead a small team of data engineers — setting direction, reviewing their work, growing them — and you will keep building yourself. You are also the person who makes our AI ambitions possible: the foundation behind our data agents and our Company Brain is yours to design and deliver.

At Destinus we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing, building advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across three European plants. The data you will work with is physical — parts, build progress, shortages, non-conformances — and the questions asked of it get harder each year as we grow. If you want a platform you can still shape rather than one already set in concrete, this is a good moment to arrive.

What You'll Do

  • Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.
  • Lead, mentor, and grow a small team of data engineers: set priorities, review code, raise the technical bar, and develop the people.
  • Stay hands-on. You will build pipelines, notebooks, and Delta tables yourself, not only direct others who do.
  • Own the integrations that land data in OneLake from our source systems — ERP, HR, shopfloor, quality, and the business applications that come after them — choosing sensibly between Data Factory pipelines, dataflows, shortcuts, and mirroring for each source.
  • Own the gold layer and the semantic models built on it, so that Power BI reads from one governed source rather than from copies scattered around the business.
  • Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence.
  • Own lineage across the estate: know what feeds what, be able to prove it to an auditor, and make dependencies visible rather than tribal knowledge.
  • Build the data foundation for our AI programme — the lakehouse structures, pipelines, and knowledge graph behind our Fabric data agents and our Company Brain — and deliver it to a standard that can be trusted with a real question.
  • Design and maintain the OneLake security and access model together with your team: workspace roles, access groups, and the controls that decide who sees what in the lake.
  • Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us.

Requirements

What You’ll Need

Requirements

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's.
  • Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. If your depth is in Azure Synapse, Databricks, or Data Lake Storage Gen2 and you have since moved onto Fabric in earnest, we will take that seriously.
  • Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does.
  • Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQL, solid PySpark, and comfort building and orchestrating pipelines yourself. This is not a role that stops at diagrams.
  • Practical understanding of Fabric capacity: how workloads consume it, how to spot what is burning it, and how to keep the platform inside its envelope.
  • Experience leading engineers — formally, or as a technical lead who set direction and mentored others. A first step into people management is welcome if the technical leadership is already there.
  • Proven integration experience with ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, as well as APIs, flat-file landings, and change data capture from operational databases.
  • Solid data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling and an understanding of how a semantic layer serves Power BI.
  • Working knowledge of lineage, data governance, and access control in a cloud platform; exposure to Microsoft Purview is a plus.
  • Interest or experience in the data foundations behind AI assistants — retrieval, knowledge graphs, and preparing data so that an agent can answer with it.
  • Aerospace or another regulated industry is an advantage; so is experience in a start-up or scale-up.
  • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.

Who You Are

You are an architect who never stops building. You have strong opinions about how a platform should be structured, and you earn the right to them by being in the code. You would rather make a design decision explicit and documented than let it live in one person's head.

You care more about reliability than novelty. You know that the measure of a data platform is whether people trust the numbers that come out of it on a Monday morning, not how modern the stack looks on a slide. When something breaks, you want to know why it was possible, not just how to patch it.

jobs.title: Senior Data & Analytics Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Data & Analytics Engineer

Looking for a new adventure? You’ve come to the right place.

We're an Amsterdam-based team of 100 (and counting) with 25+ nationalities amongst us! A varied bunch of “Citizens of The World” with a wide range of skills and hundreds of thousands of kilometers under our travel belts. And we have something important in common (other than our very well-worn passports): We want to change the way people travel.

And that's exactly what we're doing, with the travel app to plan, track, and relive trips in a smart and beautiful way.

Polarsteps has over 23 million users already, but, for us, this is just the beginning. We have big plans for the future, and so we need even more talented and enthusiastic people to help us on our journey.

Want to know more about us? Here you go.

Your expedition at Polarsteps - Senior Data & Analytics Engineer

Over the past 10+ years, Polarsteps has grown massively through word-of-mouth, thanks to our product and tech department building a top-quality user experience for all our travelers.

As our first Senior Data & Analytics Engineer, you'll own the foundation that every data-driven decision at Polarsteps is built on. Product & growth teams run experiments and analyse the data every week, leadership need clear reports for investors, and all of that depends on data that is reliable, modelled and compliant. You'll set the direction for our data platform, bring structure to data governance, and own the data infra that helps our product managers, marketers and data scientists do their job even better. You'll work closely with the Head of Engineering on infrastructure and architecture, and with the Head of Growth and product teams on what the business needs from data.

With 20M+ users and ratings of 4.8 and 4.7 on the app stores and features in multiple Google and Apple showcases, we've got an impressive past. But we're even more excited for the future, and you'll play a crucial role in building the data foundation that gets Polarsteps to 100M+ travelers around the globe.

Your itinerary

What your journey at Polarsteps will look like day-to-day.

  • Own the data platform roadmap: set the strategy for our data infrastructure and warehouse, make the build-vs-buy and tooling calls, and oversee execution together with DevOps.

  • Design, build and maintain scalable ingestion pipelines for both internal (product events, back-end data) and external sources (ad platforms, attribution, app store data).

  • Build and maintain a clean, documented modeling layer (e.g. dbt) that serves as the single source of truth for analysts, data scientists and self-serving PMs.

  • Lead data governance: define and enforce event naming and tracking standards, a schema change process, documentation, and dashboard ownership.

  • Embed privacy in the data stack: make sure personal data is categorized, minimized and pseudonymized before it reaches downstream and third-party tools, in close collaboration with Legal

  • Own the health of the stack: monitoring, alerting, data quality checks and cost management, so issues are caught before they reach stakeholders.

  • Define who owns what across our data tooling (e.g. Mixpanel, our warehouse and BI layer), and help teams get the most out of self-serve analytics.

  • Enable data enrichment to unlock deeper insights for Product and Growth.

  • Explore how we can safely use LLMs (such as Claude) on top of our data for analysis and reporting.

  • Act as the go-to data partner for Product, Engineering and Growth, and help grow the data function as Polarsteps scales.

The equipment in your backpack

What we're hoping you'll bring with you.

✅ 5+ years of experience in data engineering, analytics engineering or a hybrid data role, ideally in a B2C product or mobile app company.

✅ Strong SQL and Python, and hands-on experience modeling large event datasets in a modern warehouse (e.g. ClickHouse, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift).

✅ Experience with dbt and an orchestration tool such as Airflow or Dagster.

✅ Proven track record of bringing structure to data governance: tracking plans, event ownership, documentation and data quality.

✅ Experience with product analytics tools (e.g. Mixpanel, Amplitude) and BI tools (e.g. Metabase, Looker).

✅ Comfortable owning infrastructure decisions: cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure), infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform), CI/CD for data.

✅ A pragmatic, ownership-driven mindset: you're happy to set the strategy and get your hands dirty, and you enjoy the hygiene work others tend to avoid.

✅ Excellent communication skills: you can explain trade-offs to engineers and to non-technical stakeholders alike.

Bonus points if you have:

✨ Experience with mobile attribution or marketing data (e.g. AppsFlyer, SKAdNetwork, ad platform APIs).

✨ Experience with reverse ETL or CDPs (e.g. RudderStack, Twilio Segment).

✨ Experience with experimentation data and A/B testing infrastructure.

✨ Knowledge of GDPR and handling personal data responsibly in an analytics stack.

1st class Polarsteps extras

Some cool things to make the journey extra sweet.

  • A yearly free flight or train ride to a random location! Give our Teleporter a spin here.

  • A shiny MacBook to work your magic on.

  • Hybrid working, our way. Work from home and the office, we ask everyone to be in the office 2 days a week. It’s how we stay flexible, focused, and meaningfully connected in person.

  • An extensive home office set-up, everything from noise-canceling headphones to a standing desk.

  • 30 days of vacation (for adventures or sitting on the couch, it's up to you).

  • Two paid Culture Days for days that are important to you but not recognized by the official Dutch calendar.

  • The option to switch up your zoom background by working from another country for up to 8 weeks a year.

  • A personal development budget for that curious mind of yours!

  • A pension plan to help you save for those around-the-world retirement trips.

  • Delicious daily team lunches.

  • Awesome monthly parties, as well as team trips away.

  • A lively office in downtown Amsterdam, with travel costs reimbursed.

  • Free Polarsteps Travel Books to contain all your far-flung adventures.

At Polarsteps, we believe the best products are built by people as diverse as the travelers using our apps! That's why we specifically encourage people underrepresented in the tech industry to apply for a role with us. Because we believe that diversity, be it age, race, sexual orientation, physical ability, ethnicity, or gender identity, makes both the world and the workplace better.

jobs.title: Junior Tester
jobs.description:
Junior Tester

Ben jij nieuwsgierig naar hoe software werkt en vind je het leuk om uit te zoeken of alles doet wat het zou moeten doen? Heb je oog voor detail, stel je graag kritische vragen en krijg je energie van het vinden van verbeterpunten?

Dan is deze functie als Junior Tester precies wat je zoekt!

Als tester speel je een belangrijke rol in de kwaliteit van software. Je onderzoekt applicaties, voert testen uit en kijkt kritisch naar de werking ervan. Kom je iets tegen wat niet klopt? Dan analyseer je wat er aan de hand is en zorg je ervoor dat jouw bevindingen duidelijk bij de juiste mensen terechtkomen.

Je hoeft nog geen ervaring te hebben als tester. We vinden het vooral belangrijk dat je leergierig, analytisch en nauwkeurig bent en graag wilt ontdekken hoe je software steeds beter kunt maken.

Wat ga je doen als Junior Tester?

Als Junior Tester houd je je bezig met het controleren en beoordelen van de werking en kwaliteit van applicaties en systemen. Je werkt samen met ontwikkelaars, analisten en andere betrokken collega's om ervoor te zorgen dat software goed functioneert en voldoet aan de verwachtingen.

Je leert stap voor stap hoe je verschillende soorten testen uitvoert en hoe je bevindingen op een duidelijke manier rapporteert.

Concreet zijn jouw werkzaamheden:

  • Opstellen van testscenario's

  • Uitvoeren van testgevallen

  • Controleren of applicaties werken zoals bedoeld

  • Signaleren van fouten, afwijkingen en verbeterpunten

  • Analyseren van testresultaten en bevindingen

  • Registreren en duidelijk communiceren van bevindingen

  • Samenwerken met developers, analisten en andere stakeholders

Je krijgt gedurende het traineeship de ruimte om praktijkervaring op te doen en steeds meer verantwoordelijkheid te nemen. Zo groei je stap voor stap van trainee naar een zelfstandige tester.

Binnen het traineeship Business & IT ontwikkel je jezelf in twee jaar tijd tot een echte IT-professional. Je doet direct praktijkervaring op, volgt trainingen en behaalt relevante certificaten die je de rest van je carrière kunt gebruiken.

In het eerste jaar leg je een sterke basis in IT, systemen, processen en communicatie. Vanuit daar ontwikkel je jezelf steeds verder binnen jouw vakgebied.

jobs.title: Data analist Lenen, Sparen & Retailbeleggen
jobs.description:
Data analist Lenen, Sparen & Retailbeleggen

De afdeling Lenen, Sparen en Retailbeleggen (LSR) houdt toezicht op financiële producten en diensten voor consumenten, zoals hypotheken, kredieten, sparen, betalen en beleggen. We zorgen dat informatie duidelijk is en dat online dienstverlening goed toegankelijk is. Samen zorgen we dat het klantbelang centraal staat, vooral voor kwetsbare groepen.

 

Ons toezicht richt zich op het herkennen en aanpakken van risico’s voor consumenten. We willen dit zo snel en effectief mogelijk doen. Om meer impact te maken, gebruiken we data op een slimme manier. Daarbij zoeken we continu naar signalen, toetsen we aannames en brengen we risico’s en mogelijke blinde vlekken in beeld. Zo kunnen we sneller inspelen op veranderingen in de financiële sector.

 

De vraagstukken waar je aan werkt zijn vaak nieuw, complex en actueel. Denk aan risico’s rond Buy Now Pay Later, online beleggingsplatformen, AI-toepassingen of ontwikkelingen in de cryptomarkt. Jouw analyses dragen direct bij aan keuzes die de AFM maakt in haar toezicht.

 

Dit ga je doen:

  • Samenwerken met toezichthouders om risico’s voor consumenten tijdig te signaleren.

  • Ontwikkelen van dataproducten die inzichten vertalen naar gerichte acties.

  • Implementeren van betrouwbare en schaalbare oplossingen voor effectiever toezicht.

  • Visualiseren van resultaten in dashboards die toezichthouders ondersteunen.

  • Kansen signaleren om processen slimmer in te richten en repetitief werk te automatiseren.

  • Experimenteren met nieuwe technieken zoals AI om toezicht slimmer, sneller en effectiever te maken.

 

Team
Team Data Analyse & Innovatie is één van de vijf teams binnen de afdeling LSR. Dit team is verantwoordelijk voor het verder ontwikkelen en uitvoeren van de Datagedreven Toezicht Strategie (DGT) van LSR.

 

Dit betekent dat het team toezichtsvragen vertaalt naar oplossingen met data. We bouwen aan een stevige basis en een duidelijke planning (roadmap) voor de hele afdeling. Ook helpt het team om data echt te gaan gebruiken in het toezicht. Zo kunnen we straks beter controleren of instellingen zich aan de regels houden, risico’s inschatten en slimme technologie zoals AI inzetten om ons werk sneller en efficiënter te maken. Ook kijkt het team naar risico’s van nieuwe technologie in de financiële sector. Zo spelen we een belangrijke rol in het tijdig herkennen van risico’s.

 

De deadline voor deze vacature is 25 november 2026.


Dit vragen we:

⭐ Een afgeronde WO-opleiding, bijvoorbeeld Data Science, Business Analytics, Wiskunde, Econometrie, Technische Bedrijfskunde of een vergelijkbare (bèta) studie met een sterke analytische of statistische component.

⭐ Minimaal 2 jaar werkervaring en kennis van het data/science werkveld en de daarbij behorende tools en technieken. Hierbij is ervaring met Microsoft Power BI, SQL, Python, Azure Data Bricks een vereiste.

⭐Kennis van softwareontwikkeling, versiebeheer, codereview en unit testing is vereist.

⭐ Analytisch sterk: het vermogen om complexe datasets te analyseren, patronen te herkennen en inzichten te genereren. Je neemt informatie niet zonder meer aan, toetst aannames en identificeert risico’s, afwijkingen en mogelijke blinde vlekken.

⭐ Proactieve houding: je werkt graag samen en draagt bij aan het gezamenlijke succes, tegelijkertijd kan je zelfstandig knopen doorhakken en analyses omzetten in concrete en bruikbare uitkomsten.

⭐ Communicatieve vaardigheden: je kunt complexe technische informatie helder en beknopt overbrengen aan niet of minder-technische collega’s. Ervaring met datavisualisatie om gegevens begrijpelijk en toegankelijk te presenteren voor verschillende belanghebbenden.

 

Please note: excellent proficiency in Dutch, both verbal and written, is required for this position.

jobs.title: Research Engineer Privacy and Anonymization
jobs.description:
Research Engineer Privacy and Anonymization

Location: San Francisco or Singapore (on-site), or remote (Singapore or US Pacific time zones)
Start Date: ASAP
Languages: English
Team: Engineering

About the Role

Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. Their marketplace helps the people who create data get value for it, and gives AI labs trustworthy data to train on. It is already used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs, and the company is backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand.

We are looking for a Research Engineer, Privacy and Anonymization to build the systems that make sensitive, real-world data safe and still useful for AI training. You will develop methods to detect and remove personally identifiable information, secrets and other sensitive content from raw data before it enters processing and synthetic data pipelines â protecting privacy without destroying the structure and signal that make the data valuable for training agents.

This is a privacy and data-protection engineering seat, not a synthetic-task design role. You will own the pipeline that stands in front of downstream processing, training, evaluation and synthetic generation.

This is a full-time role, starting ASAP. Offices are in San Francisco and Singapore; remote candidates are welcome if their working hours can overlap about 70â80% with either San Francisco (US Pacific) or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring.

What You'll Do

  • Build systems to detect PII, quasi-identifiers, credentials and other sensitive information, and design transformations based on the data type and the downstream use case.

  • Develop and benchmark detection approaches that combine rules, statistical models, classifiers and LLM-based methods.

  • Build production pipelines that anonymize raw data before it enters downstream processing, training, evaluation or synthetic data generation.

  • Create evaluation frameworks that measure privacy risk and retained data utility, including recall-weighted metrics, leakage tests and adversarial re-identification attempts.

  • Design systems that stay robust to new data sources, schema drift, unusual formats and sensitive information embedded in unexpected fields.

  • Work with engineering, research, operations and customers to translate privacy requirements into practical technical policies and safeguards.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong proficiency in Python, and experience building reliable production data or machine-learning systems.

  • Experience with information extraction, named-entity recognition, classification, or related methods for detecting rare or sensitive content.

  • Strong experimental instincts, and the ability to compare approaches across recall, precision, latency, cost and downstream data utility.

  • An understanding of the difference between redaction, masking, pseudonymization, anonymization and synthetic data â and when each is appropriate.

  • High attention to detail, and the ability to reason about subtle leakage paths, edge cases and adversarial failure modes.

  • Experience building data-processing pipelines end to end, including where there was no fully prescribed roadmap.

  • Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating across teams and time zones.

  • Strong candidates may also have hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (such as differential privacy, k-anonymity, secure aggregation or format-preserving encryption); have worked with sensitive data in healthcare, finance or security; have built low-latency or high-throughput ML inference or data-processing systems; or have taken work from early research through to production.

  • Technical aptitude and learning potential matter more than years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet every point above.

Why This Role Matters for You

  • Make real-world data safe to train on: You will build the systems that let sensitive data be used for AI training without exposing people or secrets.

  • Privacy without wrecking utility: The job is not only to redact, but to keep the structure and signal that downstream training and synthetic pipelines need.

  • From detection to production: You will own the full path: detection methods, transformations, evaluation, and the pipeline that sits in front of training and generation.

  • Hard, high-stakes edge cases: Work on leakage paths, schema drift and adversarial failure modes, not only clean benchmark datasets.

  • San Francisco, Singapore, or remote: Work on-site in San Francisco or Singapore, or remotely, with hours that overlap about 70â80% with either US Pacific or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring.

Senior Customer Success Manager, Strategic

About Customer.io

Over 9,000 companies, from scrappy startups to global brands, use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data.

Hi! I’m Lauren, Senior Manager of Customer Success at Customer.io. I’m looking for a Senior Customer Success Manager, Strategic to join our Americas team and own relationships with some of our largest customers. You’ll guide each account from onboarding through renewal, tie platform use to the business results your customers care about, and partner with Account Managers, Technical Support, Product, and Engineering along the way.

What we value

  • Customer outcomes first: you connect what a customer does in Customer.io to the goals their business is trying to reach
  • Ownership: you run your book of business, watch for risk early, and decide on next steps with confidence
  • Collaboration: you work with Account Managers, Technical Support, Product, and Engineering to get customers what they need
  • Curiosity about AI: you pick up new AI functionality quickly and bring it into your conversations with customers
  • Adaptability: you handle a varied, non-verticalized book and a fast pace of change with a steady head

What you’ll do

  • Manage a book of roughly 20 to 35 Strategic customers, each above $100k in ARR, guiding them through onboarding, adoption, and long-term success
  • Link platform use to measurable business outcomes, and track results such as renewal rate and growth dollars across your book
  • Partner with Account Managers to spot and qualify expansion opportunities, shape renewal strategy, and keep customer value aligned with revenue goals
  • Lead quarterly and executive business reviews, including onsite EBRs, and build mutual success plans with senior stakeholders
  • Build relationships with several stakeholders in each account, including leaders above the day-to-day decision maker
  • Read account risk closely, dig into the signals, and decide on the best next steps, including managing escalations
  • Talk through technical needs with users, then raise the conversation to strategic impact with executive sponsors and give recommendations that keep customers renewing year after year
  • Act as a bridge between Customer Success, Technical Support, Product, and Engineering, advocating for customers and bringing fresh perspectives to the CS org

What we’re looking for

  • Based in the U.S. or Canada, and open to travel
  • 5+ years of enterprise CSM experience in SaaS, managing complex, strategic accounts
  • Hands-on commercial involvement in renewals, upsell, or expansion, with a clear grasp of gross retention and expansion drivers
  • Strategic, consultative skills: you can tie platform usage to business value and present that impact to executives through EBRs and partnership reviews
  • Comfort with APIs, integrations, and data models, enough to problem-solve at a high level without handing off every technical question
  • Influence across teams, with a track record of getting colleagues to focus on customer needs
  • Enthusiasm for AI and the urgency to keep learning new functionality as it ships

Bonus points!

  • Background in martech, CDPs, or messaging platforms
  • Spanish language skills
  • Experience running client onsites

Compensation & Benefits

We believe in transparency. Starting salary for this role is $130,000 base + 10% variable (or equivalent in local currency) depending on experience and subject to market rate adjustment. In addition to base salary, this role includes an equity grant in the form of stock options, so you share in the success you help build.

We know our people are what make us great, and we’re committed to taking great care of them. Our inclusive benefits package supports your well-being and growth, including 100% coverage of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and supplemental insurance premiums for you and your family. We also offer 16 weeks paid parental leave, unlimited PTO, stipends for remote work and wellness, a professional development budget, and more.

See full benefits here →

Our Process

No gotchas, no trick questions - just a clear, human process designed to help both of us make an informed decision.

Here's what you can expect from our hiring process:

  1. 30-minute video call with a Recruiter

  2. 45-minute video call with the Hiring Manager

All final candidates will be asked to complete a background check and employment verifications as part of our pre-employment process.

Customer.io recognizes the stifling impact of systemic injustice on diverse communities. We commit to using our influence to increase inclusion and equity within the tech industry. We strive to build an inclusive team culture, implement bias-free hiring practices, and develop community partnerships to expand our global impact.

Zoom is the only video conference platform that we use, virtual interviews will be conducted using the video capability (i.e., not via the chat), and offers will be extended in writing on official Customer.io letterhead. Please be vigilant in all of your job search activity, and if you have any questions please contact jobs@customer.io.

Join us!

Check out our careers page for more information about why you should come work with us! We believe in empathy, transparency, responsibility, and, yes, a little awkwardness. If you’re excited by what you read, apply now.

jobs.title: Country Director DACH / Managing Director Germany (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Country Director DACH / Managing Director Germany (m/w/d)

Standort: Deutschland (flexibel / hybrid)
Berichtet an: Executive Leadership Team
Verantwortungsbereich: Gesamtverantwortung für kommerzielles Wachstum, Organisationsentwicklung und Geschäftsergebnis in Deutschland in den Märkten Utility-Scale BESS sowie Community, Commercial & Industrial (CCI).

Über iwell
iwell ist ein führender europäischer Anbieter von intelligentem Energiemanagement und Batteriespeicherlösungen (Battery Energy Storage Solutions, BESS). Wir unterstützen unsere Kunden dabei, Energiekosten zu senken, den Energieverbrauch zu optimieren, ihre Resilienz zu erhöhen und die Energiewende zu beschleunigen. iwell hat eine starke Erfolgsbilanz in ganz Europa und eine etablierte Präsenz in Deutschland. Darauf aufbauend startet iwell in die nächste Wachstumsphase in einem der dynamischsten und strategisch wichtigsten Energiespeichermärkte des Kontinents.

Für diese Ambition sucht iwell eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit als Country Director / Managing Director Germany (m/w/d). Sie führen das deutsche Geschäft und treiben die weitere Expansion in zentralen Wachstumssegmenten voran.

Sie berichten direkt an das Executive Leadership Team und tragen die Gesamtverantwortung für das deutsche Geschäft. Dabei vereinen Sie kommerzielle Führung, strategische Ausrichtung, Organisationsentwicklung und operative Steuerung. Sie treiben das Vertriebswachstum selbst voran. Sie stärken die Marktposition von iwell, skalieren die lokalen Aktivitäten und erreichen ambitionierte Wachstumsziele, stets in enger Abstimmung mit der übergeordneten Gruppenstrategie.


Dies ist eine einzigartige Gelegenheit: Sie führen einen der wichtigsten Märkte in der europäischen Wachstumsstrategie von iwell und tragen direkt zur Transformation des deutschen Energiesektors bei.

Die Chance
Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Wachstum in zwei strategischen Geschäftsbereichen:
Utility-Scale BESS
Ausbau der Präsenz von iwell bei großen Batteriespeicherprojekten. Dazu gehört der Aufbau von Beziehungen zu Projektentwicklern, EPC-Unternehmen, Investoren, Energieversorgern, unabhängigen Stromerzeugern (IPPs), Übertragungs- und Verteilnetzbetreibern sowie weiteren zentralen Stakeholdern im gesamten Energie-Ökosystem.
Community, Commercial & Industrial (CCI)
Beschleunigung des Wachstums bei dezentralen Energiespeicheranwendungen. Der Fokus liegt auf Branchen wie Verkehrs- und Logistikinfrastruktur, Mobilität und Flottenelektrifizierung, Gewerbeimmobilien, Industrieanlagen, Häfen und Rechenzentren. Hinzu kommen weitere energieintensive Standorte, die mehr Resilienz, Optimierung und Nachhaltigkeit in ihrer Energieversorgung anstreben.
Ihre Aufgabe ist es, die bestehende Marktdynamik in nachhaltiges kommerzielles Wachstum umzusetzen und eine High-Performance-Kultur zu fördern. Dabei stellen Sie sicher, dass das deutsche Geschäft eng an den strategischen Zielen der Gruppe ausgerichtet bleibt.

Ihre Aufgaben
Strategische Führung

  • Entwicklung und Umsetzung der langfristigen Geschäftsstrategie für Deutschland im Einklang mit den Zielen der Gruppe und den europäischen Wachstumsambitionen.

  • Definition und Umsetzung von Wachstumsplänen für die Geschäftsbereiche Utility-Scale BESS und CCI.

  • Identifikation neuer Marktchancen, Partnerschaften, Vertriebswege und Umsatzquellen im deutschen Energie-Ökosystem.

  • Festlegung von Jahresplänen, Budgets und Wachstumszielen für das deutsche Geschäft.

  • Direkter Beitrag zu übergreifenden europäischen Wachstumsinitiativen und zur Unternehmensstrategie.

Kommerzielles Wachstum & Marktentwicklung

  • Vorantreiben der weiteren Expansion des deutschen Geschäfts von iwell in den Märkten für Großbatteriespeicher (Utility-Scale) und dezentrale Batteriespeicher.

  • Aufbau und Pflege von Beziehungen auf Senior-Ebene zu Projektentwicklern, EPCs, Energieversorgern, Aggregatoren, Infrastruktureigentümern, Investoren, strategischen Partnern sowie großen gewerblichen und industriellen Energieverbrauchern.

  • Verantwortung für die Entwicklung und Umsetzung kommerzieller Strategien, die nachhaltiges Umsatzwachstum und steigende Marktanteile sichern.

  • Identifikation und Gewinnung strategischer Partnerschaften, die die Wettbewerbsposition von iwell stärken und das Wachstum beschleunigen.

  • Repräsentation von iwell als zentrales Gesicht des Unternehmens in der sich rasant wandelnden Landschaft der deutschen Energiewende.

Geschäftsführung & Operations

  • Gesamtverantwortung für Performance und Wachstum des deutschen Geschäfts.

  • Sicherstellung operativer Exzellenz in Vertrieb, Projektabwicklung, Customer Success, Service und Support.

  • Etablierung wirksamer Strukturen für Governance, Performance-Management und Reporting.

  • Steuerung von Budgetierung, Forecasting, Ressourcenplanung und Profitabilitätszielen.

  • Regelmäßige Berichterstattung an das Executive Leadership Team zur Geschäftsentwicklung und zu Markteinblicken.

Teamführung

  • Aufbau, Führung und Weiterentwicklung einer leistungsstarken deutschen Organisation, die ambitionierte Wachstumspläne tragen kann.

  • Rekrutierung, Mentoring und Bindung herausragender Talente in kommerziellen, operativen und kundennahen Funktionen.

  • Förderung einer Kultur von Verantwortung, Zusammenarbeit, Kundenorientierung und Exzellenz.

  • Sichtbare und inspirierende Führung mit unternehmerischer und hands-on Arbeitsweise.

Markt- & Stakeholder-Engagement

  • Vertretung von iwell auf Branchenkonferenzen, bei Kundenterminen, in Regierungsforen und in Branchenverbänden.

  • Aufbau von Beziehungen zu zentralen Stakeholdern im gesamten Ökosystem der deutschen Energiewende.

  • Fundiertes und aktuelles Verständnis von Marktentwicklungen, Regulierung, Trends im Energiespeicherbereich, Flexibilitätsmärkten und neuen Chancen.

Ihr Profil
Wir suchen eine erfahrene Führungspersönlichkeit, etwa als Country Leader, Managing Director, General Manager oder Senior Commercial Executive. Sie verbinden strategische Weitsicht mit ausgeprägtem kommerziellem Gespür und können Unternehmen im deutschen Energiewendesektor skalieren.

Erfahrung & Qualifikationen

  • Umfangreiche Führungserfahrung in den Bereichen Batteriespeicher, erneuerbare Energien, dezentrale Energie, Energieinfrastruktur, Ladeinfrastruktur für E-Mobilität, Flexibilitätsdienstleistungen, Smart Energy, Energiesysteme oder in angrenzenden Branchen.

  • Fundierte Erfahrung in relevanten Kundensegmenten wie Transport, Logistik, Flottenelektrifizierung, Gewerbeimmobilien sowie Co-Location von erneuerbaren Energien und BESS.

  • Nachweisliche Erfolge in der Führung einer Ländergesellschaft, eines Geschäftsbereichs, einer regionalen Organisation oder einer wachstumsstarken kommerziellen Einheit.

  • Nachweisliche Erfolge in der Entwicklung und Umsetzung von Wachstumsstrategien.

  • Fundiertes Verständnis des deutschen Energiemarkts, des regulatorischen Umfelds und der kommerziellen Dynamik.

  • Erfahrung im Vertrieb komplexer technischer Lösungen und infrastrukturbasierter Energieprodukte.

  • Starkes Netzwerk unter Projektentwicklern, Energieversorgern, EPCs, Investoren, Aggregatoren, gewerblichen und industriellen Kunden sowie weiteren Akteuren der Energiewende.

  • Nachgewiesene Fähigkeit, leistungsstarke Teams aufzubauen und zu führen.

  • Erfahrung in der Steuerung von Geschäftsergebnissen, Budgets, Forecasts und kommerziellen Zielen.

  • Verhandlungssichere Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse.

Persönliche Eigenschaften

  • Strategisch denkende und kommerziell versierte Führungskraft.

  • Unternehmerisch, wachstumsorientiert und hands-on.

  • Hohe Glaubwürdigkeit und die Fähigkeit, Senior Stakeholder intern wie extern zu überzeugen.

  • Ergebnisorientiert, mit ausgeprägten analytischen Fähigkeiten und Entscheidungsstärke.

  • Leidenschaft für die Energiewende und technologiegetriebene Innovation.

Warum iwell?

  • Führung eines der strategisch wichtigsten europäischen Märkte von iwell.

  • Aufbau auf einer etablierten Plattform und starker Marktdynamik, mit der Chance, die nächste Wachstumsphase aktiv mitzugestalten.

  • Eine führende Rolle bei der Beschleunigung der deutschen Energiewende durch innovative Batteriespeicherlösungen.

  • Einfluss auf die Strategie auf deutscher und europäischer Ebene, in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Executive Leadership Team.

  • Langfristige Wertschöpfung durch das Wachstum einer äußerst ambitionierten und unternehmerischen Organisation.

  • Attraktives Vergütungspaket auf Executive-Niveau mit wettbewerbsfähigem Grundgehalt, leistungsabhängigem Bonus und Beteiligung an der langfristigen Wertsteigerung.

Interesse geweckt?
