Account Director
jobs.description:
Account Director

About TTC Global

Since 2004, TTC Global has helped high-profile organizations improve the quality of the software they depend on. We are an independent quality engineering and software testing consultancy operating across the US, Canada, the UK, India, Australia and New Zealand. Our work covers test automation, performance engineering, AI-First Quality Engineering and quality transformation for complex enterprise estates, with deep specialization in SAP, Oracle, Salesforce and Workday environments. TTC Global is a long-standing Tricentis partner and has been recognized by Tricentis on the global stage.

Perks of working for TTC

  • Competitive base salary and uncapped commission
  • Medical, dental and vision benefits
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid time off and paid holidays
  • Work-life balance and a relaxed, collaborative work environment
  • Growth and development opportunities

Position summary

The Account Director owns TTC Global's revenue in their region. You will grow a portfolio of existing enterprise clients, win new logos, and run the full sales cycle from first conversation through scoping, proposal, negotiation and signature. You will work alongside our delivery leaders to shape engagements that solve real quality problems, and you will be the senior relationship holder for each account after the contract is signed.

This is a quota-carrying role reporting to the Group Chief Revenue Officer. You will be supported by a Business Development Representative who books qualified meetings into your calendar, by marketing for events and campaigns, and by our partner teams at Tricentis and other platform vendors.

Responsibilities

  • Own a regional territory of named enterprise and upper mid-market accounts, with a target account list agreed each half-year.
  • Grow existing accounts by expanding from one program or platform to others (for example, from an SAP S/4HANA migration into Salesforce or Workday testing).
  • Win new logos through your own network, BDR-sourced meetings, partner referrals and events.
  • Build relationships with CIOs, VPs of IT, QA and test leaders, and program and transformation leaders.
  • Lead discovery and shape solutions with TTC delivery and practice leads, including Quality Maturity Assessments, test automation programs, Quality Engineering Managed Services and staff augmentation.
  • Write and present proposals, statements of work and RFP responses, and lead commercial negotiation.
  • Work with Tricentis and other partner account teams to co-sell and surface opportunities.
  • Keep pipeline, forecast and account plans current in HubSpot, and report on them in weekly pipeline reviews.
  • Act as the executive point of contact on live engagements, run quarterly business reviews, and escalate delivery risks early.
  • Represent TTC Global at industry events, user groups and client meetings in your region.
  • Coach the BDR on messaging, target accounts and meeting quality.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of B2B sales or account management experience, with at least 5 years selling IT services, consulting or managed services to enterprise clients.
  • A track record of meeting or exceeding an annual quota of $2M+ in services revenue.
  • Experience closing multi-year, six- and seven-figure services engagements with long sales cycles and procurement involvement.
  • An existing network of IT and QA decision makers in the region.
  • Exposure to software testing, quality engineering, DevOps or enterprise platforms (SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, Workday, Guidewire) is strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of HubSpot or Salesforce CRM and Microsoft Office.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
  • Authorized to work in the United States.

Competencies and skills

  • Consultative selling: connects a client's business risk to a practical quality engineering solution.
  • Account growth: builds multi-threaded relationships and expands accounts over several years.
  • Commercial acumen: comfortable with pricing, margin, rate cards and contract terms.
  • Executive presence: credible with CIOs and senior technology leaders.
  • Self-direction: organized, disciplined and productive working remotely within a small regional team.

Location and travel

  • Remote within the region, with a preference for candidates near [region's main metro].
  • Travel up to 30% for client meetings and industry events, mainly within the region.

Success markers (12-month outlook)

  • Full account plans in place for every named account within 90 days.
  • A qualified pipeline of at least 3x annual quota within six months.
  • Two or more new enterprise logos signed in the first year.
  • Growth in revenue from the existing account base year over year.

If your experience or qualifications are similar to our ideal of a successful candidate, please consider applying. Experience comes in many ways; skills may be transferred, but passion for your career can't be substituted. At TTC, we understand the importance of diversity and how much value it brings to the table. Diversity brings about creativity and new perspectives, which is why we encourage everyone to apply.

Full-Time USA

jobs.description:
Senior Sales Compensation Manager

At ClickUp, we're building the future of work: the first truly converged AI workspace unifying tasks, docs, chat, calendar, and enterprise search, all supercharged by context-driven AI. We are an AI-native company. Every team member is expected to leverage AI daily, and we evaluate AI fluency as part of our hiring process. Join us and help redefine what's possible. 🚀

ClickUp's mission is to make the world more productive. As we build an all-in-one productivity platform that helps teams plan and do their best work, dependable sales incentives help our go-to-market teams stay focused on customers and growth. The Senior Sales Compensation Manager sits at the intersection of Finance, Sales, and Revenue Operations, making variable pay accurate, understandable, and dependable.

The Role

  • Own the monthly commission calculation process for sales roles, translating approved plan rules and sales data into accurate payout results delivered on schedule.

  • Reconcile source data and compensation-system records, investigate discrepancies, and document calculations and adjustments so payout results are clear and auditable.

  • Own the investigation and resolution of complex commission exceptions, identify root causes, and partner across Finance, Sales, Revenue Operations, and Payroll to implement lasting improvements to processes and controls.

  • Experience using AI tools and building AI-powered workflows to streamline sales compensation calculations, reconciliations, and reporting, with the ability to validate outputs for accuracy and protect confidential compensation data.

  • Strong Excel or spreadsheet skills, including working with detailed datasets, formulas, reconciliations, and error checks.

  • Careful, methodical approach to validating inputs, tracing variances, documenting assumptions, and protecting confidential compensation information.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain calculations and policy details to sales and finance partners in plain language.

jobs.title: Customer Support Operations
jobs.description:
Customer Support Operations

I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy.

I started Anima to change that.

Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima.

We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions.

Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them.

If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives.

-- Shun

£25k–£75k base, depending on location and experience, plus equity
Remote, UK time zone

The role

When a clinic gets stuck, you’ll help them move forward. You’ll become an expert in Anima, untangle technical problems and give clinicians and practice teams clear, practical answers.

This is a hands-on IC role with real ownership of how support develops at Anima. You’ll resolve customer issues while helping build the function: deciding what to measure, improving how the team works and shaping what excellent support looks like as we scale.

What you’ll do

  • Own issues through to resolution. Support customers through Intercom, email and short video calls. Investigate thoroughly, keep people informed and follow through.

  • Make technical problems actionable. Reproduce bugs and give engineers clear steps, relevant logs and customer impact. Help distinguish product issues from gaps in understanding or setup.

  • Make answers easier to find. Turn useful solutions into Help Centre articles, internal guidance and short walkthroughs.

  • Build the support function. Identify what’s holding the team back and own improvements—from how we measure quality and prioritise work to the systems, playbooks and automations we use. Test new approaches, see whether they work and help the whole team improve.

  • Bring customer insight into the business. Help Product understand where users struggle, and work with Implementation and Customer Success when an issue needs broader attention.

Success means customers get accurate answers quickly, issues reach a clear resolution, and the team gets better at preventing or handling the next one.

What you’ll bring

  • Practical problem-solving. Evidence of getting to the bottom of unfamiliar problems, testing possible explanations and finding a workable solution.

  • Clear, empathetic communication. The ability to explain a complicated issue simply, adapt to different levels of technical confidence and build trust with frustrated customers.

  • High agency and drive. Examples of improving a process or building something useful—and seeing it through.

  • Reliability under pressure. Good judgement about urgency, careful follow-through and the ability to manage several conversations without losing track.

  • Curiosity about how products work. An appetite for learning Anima in depth and working closely with engineers to resolve problems.

Relevant experience could come from customer support, technical operations, implementation or another role involving complex products and direct customer interaction. Experience with support platforms or process automation is useful; your judgement and results matter more than familiarity

What we offer

Anima should be where you do your life’s best work. We support that with:

  • Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 UK public holidays, with flexible additional time off.

  • Health cover: private medical, dental, vision and mental health insurance.

  • Parental leave: 12 weeks’ maternity leave at full pay, rising to 24 weeks after two years; 4 weeks’ paternity leave at full pay.

  • Pension: 4% employer contributions, with salary sacrifice and 100% of the employer National Insurance savings passed on to you.

  • Learning: £1,000 annual budget for your development.

  • Fitness: gym subscription matching up to £50 per month.

  • Equipment: a high-spec MacBook and a home office budget.

  • Time together: two full-team off-sites each year, previous destinations include Mykonos and Mexico.

  • Farringdon office: a beautiful new London HQ, with most of the team together at least twice a week.

Everyone is welcome at Anima. We strongly believe in building a diverse and inclusive team. If you’re excited by our mission and believe you could do this work well, we’d love to hear from you, even if your experience doesn’t match every point above. If adjustments would help you participate fully in the interview process, please let us know.

Full-Time UK

jobs.title: Technical Lead - Golang
jobs.description:
Technical Lead - Golang

This is a permanent, full-time remote opportunity open to candidates based in the UK. While the role is primarily remote, occasional travel to client sites across the UK may be required to attend meetings, workshops and other project-related activities.

About Nearform

Nearform is an independent team of data & AI experts, engineers, and designers who build intelligent digital solutions and capability at pace. We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact.

Our deep expertise in solving the world’s most complex digital problems, along with our collaborative, people-first approach, enables enterprises to build breakthrough products and modernise legacy systems by unleashing the power of AI.

Today, our team of 500 experts in 20+ countries is trusted by leading enterprises including Lululemon, Puma, Sun Life, Starbucks, Travelex, Virgin Media 02, and Walmart.

As part of our Engineering function, you will work closely with clients to translate complex business requirements into innovative digital products.

Whether you are a Senior Engineer, Tech Lead, or DevOps Engineer, you will collaborate with distributed teams, leveraging cutting-edge technologies to build secure, high-performance applications. Our Nearform engineers are known for building high quality, scalable solutions that solve real world problems.

About the Technical Lead Role:

As a Technical Lead at Nearform, you will be responsible for leading and guiding development teams while working directly with clients to translate business and technical requirements into impactful applications. However, as you’ll likely work on a variety of projects in your time here, your responsibilities may also include:

  • Provide technical and line-management leadership to your development team.
  • Take responsibility for the successful delivery of projects.
  • Identify and resolve blockers before they become issues.
  • Ensure best practices in software development, DevOps, and agile methodologies are upheld within the team.
  • Work directly with clients, translating requirements into technical briefs.
  • Shape and define architectural decisions ensuring scalability, security, and maintainability.
  • Provide updates to client and Nearform leadership to ensure clear understanding of project status and drive good decision-making.

What we are looking for in this person:

  • Significant experience in software engineering as either a Senior Engineer leading projects and mentoring or as a Technical Lead. For this particular role, you will ideally be using Golang, experience with additional other languages such as JavaScript or Python would be desirable.
  • Experience working directly with clients or customers to understand technical requirements.
  • Experience leading software engineering teams through technical delivery and either direct line management or mentoring.
  • Deep understanding of agile ways of working, best practices and design patterns.
  • Deep understanding of test-driven development and testing best practices.
  • Deep understanding of version control tools, e.g. Git.
  • Understanding of DevOps practices and cloud technologies (AWS, Azure, GCP)
  • Understanding of operational concerns (such as monitoring, performance testing, security considerations, accessibility, GDPR)
  • Empathy and people skills
  • Financial services industry experience

Benefits and Perks we offer at Nearform

  • Annual Company Bonus - We all help Nearform to hit company goals so we all receive a share of the profits on an annual basis in line with company performance.
  • Work Remotely and Flexibly - We have a genuine dedication to work/life balance. Our flexible working culture allows you to work around what matters - school run, no problem!
  • Paid Time Off Package - We offer an annual leave of 25 days plus public holidays. We also offer sick leave, marriage leave and many more.
  • Remote Working Allowance - Every 2 years, you will have a budget of up to €1250 (equivalent in GBP) to help you set up a comfortable and productive workspace in addition to your essential equipment provided by Nearform when you join.
  • Training and Development Allowance - Nearform is committed to supporting and investing in employees’ ongoing learning and professional development. You will be encouraged to pursue relevant learning opportunities that support your growth and the growth of others, subject to manager approval.
  • Healthcare - It’s important to always take care of your health, so we offer additional private healthcare here at Nearform. If you wish to learn more about the plan offered feel free to reach out to our team.
  • Pension & Insurances - We offer a pension match of up to 5% and Income Protection and Death in Service for peace of mind.

Our Interview Process

Talent Call (30 mins via Zoom)
An initial conversation with a member of our Talent Team to explore your background, leadership experience, and career goals. We’ll provide an overview of Nearform, discuss potential alignment, and answer any questions you may have. This step helps us assess initial alignment.

Technical Lead Assessment (90 mins, Zoom)
A structured assessment led by a senior Technical Lead or Head of Engineering, designed to evaluate key aspects of a Technical Lead role. This session includes a selection of tasks to cover:

Architecture Design – We want to see how you approach a high level problem, demonstrating your design thinking and decision-making process.
Technical Implementation – How do you turn a design into reality, taking into account business needs?
Code Standards and Feedback – We want to see not just your own skills, but also how you improve those around you

Hiring Manager Interview (45 mins via Zoom)
A conversation with a Hiring Manager focused on your approach to teamwork, client collaboration, and problem-solving in an enterprise development setting. We'll also share more details about Nearform and the potential projects you may join.

There may also be an additional interview with the client depending on the project.

Ready to Join Us?

If you're passionate about building high-quality applications, solving complex challenges, and driving innovation in enterprise development, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now via our careers page at Nearform and be part of a team that values technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.

Nearform is committed to shaping a better world in all that we do. Our global team is built based on respect, inclusivity, diversity and excellence.

If you require any adjustments to the interview process as part of your application, please let someone from our Talent Team know so they can help.

We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions.

Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them.

If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives.

-- Shun

Do you want to save lives with every clinic that you onboard?

Please note that as this role may involve site work and on-site support for our users, we can only consider your application if you are based in the UK. You will not be able to complete our screening task if you are not based in the UK, so please bear this in mind when submitting your application. We hope to welcome you to the team soon!

Join Anima, and you'll use your influence and people skills to get Anima into clinics and entire regions: an urgently needed product that saves lives amid critical levels of patient demand, with healthcare systems in crisis across the globe.

Since launching in the UK, we're now used in by GP practices, primary care networks and federations across the country who collectively provide care for over 2 million patients.

Have amazing stakeholder conversations with users who fanatically love the product, and steer our product direction

Our current distribution team have said that one of the biggest perks of working at Anima is seeing the delight and disbelief on people’s faces when we show them our demo, something that is truly a 10x generational leap. Here’s what some of our users have been saying:

*“I sent a plan to the patient and it’s incredible, within a few minutes they’re coming back to me saying that they can make the appointment!”

"I would call that next generation, I think you have that badge"

”Sometimes you need to stop driving a Fiesta and buy a Mercedes"*

Lots of us went into medicine because we wanted to maximise our positive impact. At Anima, we understand that distribution is the other half of a legendary product. Here are incredible things we’ve built as a result of our fullstack sales team:

  • A Clinical Director at one of our practices wanted to streamline multiple access channels and make access equitable and fair. After some great discovery and deep listening, the AM together with the customer suggested we build something called ‘proxy requests’, which would allow the reception team at a clinic to complete Anima requests on behalf of a patient who was on a landline call - this made it possible to give someone with no internet or mobile phone the same access to care. This is now one of our most popular features that has led to viral referrals and fanatical users.

  • One of our fullstack account manager, realised that adding a configurable feature that allows patients to self-book appointments directly into the electronic health record calendar would be critical to closing large enterprise accounts. By deeply understanding the pain points and anxieties underlying the feature, Anima built the feature in 9 days, to the great excitement of users at demo calls and $1m+ ACV meetings.

  • Off the back of fanatical referrals from our existing users, the team was invited to present to NHS England at national and regional level, and we’ve been helping to shape the future of the primary care market through an upcoming $1bn+ procurement framework.

Does this sound like you?

  • Hungry and wants their shot to change the world - a force of nature when empowered with the tools, resources and development to do it.

  • Exceptional communicator, able to distill complex information into clear and concise bullets without jargon. An excellent conduit between users and the rest of the company.

  • Able to execute a high sigma discovery process and in combination with incisive people intuition, elucidate deep pain points and opportunities to excite within minutes of the first call.

  • Has incredibly high standards for themselves and an unshakeable growth mindset: able to challenge themselves and those around them to push to do things better.

  • Exceptionally organised: able to build & maintain multiple relationships across a diverse range of organisations, and consistently execute on plans to onboard and retain users. Reliably follows up on 100% of qualified leads at optimal intervals.

  • A gifted relationship builder, able to quickly build rapport and emotional anchors with almost anyone and any persona.

  • Pragmatic rather than dogmatic in decision making: able to weigh real world data appropriately, changing course when necessary towards optimal outcomes for patients and clinicians.

  • Keen to understand the big picture & entire context of the company and vertical; impatient to grow towards a senior executive role.

  • Seeks to maximise combined team productivity, communicating the right things at the right time through the right channels.

  • Intellectually curious and loves learning - able to tackle entirely novel challenges that lack prior precedent through first principles thinking, creatively using the right pragmatic approach, with an understanding of alternatives and trade offs.

It's helpful to have B2B/SaaS experience, generating leads of $10k+ ACV, but not mandatory - we will make exceptions if you’re a high performing BDR. You need to have demonstrated a high growth mindset and potential for rapid skill development through past projects. For this role, you will need to be based in the UK.

Our current users & what to expect from the role

We're live with GP teams across the country, being used by teams across the NHS. Over the rest of 2024, we're continuing to onboard teams that want to build the future of healthcare, and will be working with the NHS to deploy Anima at regional & national level. We’ll also be identifying international partners to power Anima’s next stage of growth.

We’re looking to add talented account executives who understand the urgency and importance of what we’re doing for society and are hungry to make impact.

Our VP Sales has a 90%+ e2e close rate, and the distro org averages about 80%. Our CAC payback, gross margin, retention are all world class and you'll be joining an exceptional team with top metrics for SaaS, despite being in a traditionally slower vertical.

First month - some examples of what to expect:

  • Participate in user discovery & demo calls to develop a deep understanding of their fundamental motivations and needs/pain points, translating these insights into optimal feature roadmaps.

  • Source leads and execute campaigns. Get as much exposure as possible to developing the full lifecycle of an opportunity from lead through to closure.

  • Join the team at events & conferences, speaking to potential users, conducting demos and converting leads.

Next 6 months - some examples of what to expect:

  • Build domain expertise to scale our prospecting, identifying the teams in the most pain who are likely to become fanatical users of Anima.

  • Become the central point of contact for assigned GP practices and PCNs. Your job is to maximise discounted fanaticism, doing whatever is necessary to help practices start - and continue - using Anima.

  • Work with customer success colleagues to maximise virality and fanaticism across your accounts, doing whatever is needed to ensure every account leads to the maximum number of fanatical referrals.

6+ months - some examples of what to expect:

  • Potential to transition into a Strategic Enterprise AE, with managerial responsibility for junior AEs joining the team.

  • Take on account management responsibility for larger accounts e.g. GP federations and ICSs (covering 1m+ patients).

  • Work with the team to scale our sales & marketing, including working with NHS leaders to identify and secure regional & national-level procurement opportunities, including those beyond primary care.

What we offer

Anima should be where you do your life’s best work. We support that with:

  • Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 UK public holidays, with flexible additional time off.

  • Health cover: private medical, dental, vision and mental health insurance.

  • Parental leave: 12 weeks’ maternity leave at full pay, rising to 24 weeks after two years; 4 weeks’ paternity leave at full pay.

  • Pension: 4% employer contributions, with salary sacrifice and 100% of the employer National Insurance savings passed on to you.

  • Learning: £1,000 annual budget for your development.

  • Fitness: gym subscription matching up to £50 per month.

  • Equipment: a high-spec MacBook and a home office budget.

  • Time together: two full-team off-sites each year, previous destinations include Mykonos and Mexico.

  • Farringdon office: a beautiful new London HQ, with most of the team together at least twice a week.

Everyone is welcome at Anima. We strongly believe in building a diverse and inclusive team. If you’re excited by our mission and believe you could do this work well, we’d love to hear from you, even if your experience doesn’t match every point above. If adjustments would help you participate fully in the interview process, please let us know.

Data Analyst, Regulatory Analytics and Reporting

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

 

We're looking for a Data Analyst, Regulatory Analytics and Reporting to join our team remotely! The #1 goal of this role is to turn complex compliance and regulatory data into clear, actionable insights that protect the business, satisfy regulators, and support senior leadership in making high-stakes decisions. You'll work at the intersection of data engineering, regulatory reporting, and compliance operations in a fast-paced, high-scrutiny environment where accuracy and audit-readiness are non-negotiable.

Beyond technical expertise, success in this role depends on being a true business partner who combines data-driven insights with deep knowledge of compliance regulations and frameworks. You'll own end-to-end data management from building and maintaining datasets and pipelines to designing dashboards and insights for compliance and leadership teams. You will also automate compliance processes and workflows to boost efficiency and minimize human error.

If you combine exceptional data analysis expertise with solid knowledge of compliance regulations, a keen eye for regulatory risk, and the drive to shape the future of crypto with a top-tier brand - this is your next mission!

 

The opportunity

  • Own the design of dashboards, compliance metrics, and regulatory reports, turning data into actionable insights for stakeholders, cross-functional partners, and regional compliance officers

  • Automate end to end compliance related data solutions, governance controls, and automations to boost efficiency and minimize manual intervention

  • Dive into large, complex datasets to turn findings into scalable, audit-ready data models that facilitate regulatory reporting and analytics

  • Translate regulatory and business requests into accurate reports and automated data pipelines using Python, SQL, DBT and Airflow

  • Lead cross-functional projects with analysts, engineers, and compliance teams to build and maintain high-quality data pipelines and sources

  • Coordinate client data quality monitoring by identifying issues, flagging remediations, and partnering with responsible teams to ensure timely resolution

  • Support ad-hoc data requests for audits, exams, risk assessments, and day-to-day business needs

  • Deliver insights that shape compliance direction through clear, data-driven storytelling

 

What you bring

  • 5+ years of experience in data analysis and data management within financial services or a regulated industry, with hands-on experience in compliance and regulatory reporting across frameworks such as AML, KYC, Sanctions, MiCA, or MiFID

  • Solid understanding of regulatory risk and the ability to operate effectively in high-scrutiny, audit-ready environments

  • Expert SQL skills including complex joins, CTEs, and analytical functions, paired with proficiency in Python libraries such as pandas, matplotlib, and plotly

  • Hands-on experience using dbt or similar tooling to model and organize high fidelity data for reporting and decision-making

  • Experience setting up and managing data pipelines with a strong understanding of data workflow orchestration

  • Proficiency with BI and data visualization tools such as QuickSight, Power BI, or Superset to build executive-facing dashboards

  • Strong communicator who can simplify complex data ideas for both technical and non-technical audiences

  • Alignment with the values outlined in Kraken's Tentaclements document

 

Nice to haves

  • Degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Information Systems, or a related technical field

  • Passion for continuous learning and approaching problems with a beginner's mindset

  • Solid understanding of the cryptocurrency space and how financial markets function

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. jobs.title: Sales Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
Sales Operations Analyst

About Clipboard

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

About the Role

Clipboard is looking for a Sales Operations Analyst to help build and run the systems behind our sales organization.

You'll work across Salesforce, data, automation, and internal tools to help our sales team operate more effectively. That might mean building an automation that eliminates a recurring workflow, investigating a messy data problem, redesigning part of our Salesforce setup, or building a new system from the ground up.

We are a small team with an unusual operating model. Much of our execution runs through AI agents that we direct and quality-check, allowing each analyst to operate with the leverage of a much larger team.

This is equal parts builder and operator. You'll own systems end to end, work through ambiguous requests from reps and leadership, and be accountable for making sure the things you build actually work.

What You'll Do

  • Own live systems. Take ownership of production systems such as account distribution, deal intelligence, competitor tracking, and data sync pipelines. You'll be accountable for their accuracy and reliability.

  • Solve ambiguous problems. Work through requests from sales reps, managers, and leadership, figure out what is actually needed, and execute quickly.

  • Direct AI agents. Write specs and prompts, supervise AI agents, and rigorously QA their output before it touches production data.

  • Build automations and tools. Create scripts, scheduled jobs, Slack bots, and lightweight web apps that turn recurring manual work into scalable systems.

  • Analyze and report. Use SQL and other tools to answer important revenue questions and build reporting the organization can trust.

  • Guard data quality. Handle merges, deduplication, account mapping, enrichment, and other work required to keep our systems accurate at scale.

What We're Looking For

  • Evidence of building. You've built scripts, automations, tools, systems, or other solutions to real problems.

  • AI-native working style. You already use AI to multiply your output and understand where it can fail and how to verify its work.

  • High judgment under ambiguity. You can take a loosely defined problem, figure out what matters, and know when to act versus when to ask.

  • Strong attention to detail. You're comfortable being the last line of defense before changes affect production systems and large datasets.

  • Bias to ownership. When something you own breaks, you don't just fix the immediate issue. You look for the underlying problem and improve the system.

SQL and Python experience are strong pluses, but we're more interested in your curiosity, judgment, and ability to ship than checking every technical box.

Nice to Have

  • Salesforce administration or development experience, including flows, SOQL, or data model design.

  • Experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Business Operations, analytics, or a similar environment.

  • Experience building automations with tools, scripts, APIs, or AI agents.

Interview Process

  1. Application Review – We'll review your experience and evidence of things you've built, automated, or owned.

  2. Take-Home Assessment – A practical, ~2-hour assessment using a fictional company, mock website, and CRM. You'll have 48 hours to complete it, and AI tools are encouraged.

  3. Technical Walkthrough – A 30-minute session where you'll demo what you built, explain your decisions, and make a small live change to your system.

  4. Manager Interview – A 30-minute conversation focused on communication, ownership, judgment, and how you operate under ambiguity.

  5. Final Steps / Offer! – Some candidates may have an executive conversation, followed by references and an offer.

What We Offer

  • Competitive base salary

  • Insurance benefits + 401k options

  • Unlimited PTO and flexible holidays

  • Remote-first working environment

To get a better understanding of the general type of people we want to hire, you can check out our blog here.

Quick Note on Scammers:

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here.

Full-Time Canada, USA

jobs.title: Implementation Specialist
jobs.description:
Implementation Specialist

I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy.

I started Anima to change that.

Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima.

We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions.

Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them.

If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives.

-- Shun

£65k–£90k base, plus equity
UK remote, UK working hours, with occasional UK customer visits

The role

Help GP practices make a confident start with Anima.

Last quarter, we onboarded 131 practices. We’re building a dedicated Implementation team to support that growth, and you’ll be one of its first members.

You’ll own each implementation from kick-off through go-live and early support, helping practice teams build the skills and confidence to use Anima independently. You’ll also help shape how we implement: improving workflows, developing training and building a playbook that works across hundreds of practices.

What you’ll do

  • Own implementations from start to finish. Coordinate kick-off, configuration and go-live, aiming to get most practices live within their first week.

  • Make Anima work for each practice. Understand how their team operates and configure workflows around their needs.

  • Teach people to use it confidently. Run clear, practical training for clinicians and practice teams, adapting your approach to different levels of technical confidence.

  • Build confidence beyond go-live. Develop practice super users, provide 1–2 weeks of hypercare and hand over cleanly to Support and Customer Success.

  • Make great implementation repeatable. Create reusable training and group webinars. Use feedback from customers, Support and CS to solve recurring problems at their source.

What you’ll bring

  • SaaS experience. You’ve worked directly with customers on a SaaS product in onboarding, implementation or training.

  • Strong teaching and communication skills. You can make something unfamiliar feel manageable and check that people can put it into practice.

  • Patience and adaptability. You respond thoughtfully when someone is struggling or their priorities change.

  • Practical problem-solving. You learn products quickly and can work out why a workflow isn’t delivering the intended result.

  • Ownership and organisation. You can keep several implementations moving while making the next steps clear to everyone involved.

Healthcare experience isn’t required—we’ll help you learn primary care. Experience creating training videos, guides or webinars would be useful.

What we offer

Anima should be where you do your life’s best work. We support that with:

  • Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 UK public holidays, with flexible additional time off.

  • Health cover: private medical, dental, vision and mental health insurance.

  • Parental leave: 12 weeks’ maternity leave at full pay, rising to 24 weeks after two years; 4 weeks’ paternity leave at full pay.

  • Pension: 4% employer contributions, with salary sacrifice and 100% of the employer National Insurance savings passed on to you.

  • Learning: £1,000 annual budget for your development.

  • Fitness: gym subscription matching up to £50 per month.

  • Equipment: a high-spec MacBook and a home office budget.

  • Time together: two full-team off-sites each year, previous destinations include Mykonos and Mexico.

  • Farringdon office: a beautiful new London HQ, with most of the team together at least twice a week.

Everyone is welcome at Anima. We strongly believe in building a diverse and inclusive team. If you’re excited by our mission and believe you could do this work well, we’d love to hear from you, even if your experience doesn’t match every point above. If adjustments would help you participate fully in the interview process, please let us know.

Full-Time UK

Our open-source toolkit has been downloaded 97M+ times and is used by 90% of the Fortune 1000. We power production AI workflows across commercial and federal sectors — transforming PDFs, HTML, Word docs, images, emails, and more into AI-ready data pipelines that scale.

We're not just building tools; we're building the backbone of generative AI and the infrastructure that unlocks intelligence across industries.

About the Role

Unstructured is looking for Staff and Principal Software Engineers to define the architectural foundation for how enterprises process and transform unstructured data for large-language-model (LLM) applications.

This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who thrives in deep systems work—someone who could write the book on Kubernetes, lives and breathes Python, and understands Postgres at the index and transaction-log level. You’ll own the technical direction for our core platform, guiding how data moves through every layer—from ingestion to transformation to retrieval.

You’ll partner closely with the Head of Engineering, Head of Infrastructure, and product leaders to ensure Unstructured’s systems are performant, resilient, and ready to support the next generation of AI-driven workloads.

Location(s) Preferred: San Francisco, Bay Area, San Jose, Seattle, Sacramento

What You’ll Own & Drive

  • Define and evolve the end-to-end architecture for Unstructured’s data transformation and retrieval platform.

  • Build and scale distributed systems that process massive volumes of unstructured data across diverse formats and sources.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (AppSec)
jobs.description:
Senior Software Engineer (AppSec)

About us

Trigger.dev is the platform for running reliable AI agents and workflows. Developers use it to build, deploy, and scale production systems with built-in tools for orchestration, scheduling, monitoring, and debugging.

Our Cloud product is a managed service where we deploy our users’ code and auto-scale from zero to millions of executions. Today, we serve thousands of teams building AI apps and agents, handling hundreds of millions of executions per month.

About the role

You’ll own security at Trigger.dev: our infrastructure, our app, the runtime that runs our users’ code, and the secrets they trust us with.

Some of our customers let their own users run code on Trigger.dev (think coding agents running whatever instructions they’re given). That code must never reach our systems or our customers’ systems. Keeping it contained is a feature we ship, so this is a product engineering role as much as a security one.

About half to three quarters of your time will be backend engineering. The rest is hunting for problems and fixing them. When you find something, you own the fix. You’ll set your own priorities and work with others when necessary.

We’re looking for an application security (AppSec) engineer who builds: a senior backend engineer who brings a security mindset to everything they ship.

What you’ll do

  • Sandbox and runtime security. Design and harden the environments that isolate untrusted user code. This is the core of the role.

  • Security features for customers. Build things like end-to-end encrypted secrets, log redaction, private networking, and runtime hardening.

  • Automated offensive testing. Use AI tools to attack our own systems on a schedule, find weak spots, and fix them. Bring in outside pen testers when it’s worth it.

  • Detection and response. Build monitoring and alerting for suspicious activity, improve our security observability, and lead the response when something needs a look.

  • Vulnerability management. Run scanning and triage, own our vulnerability disclosure program, and handle incoming reports.

  • Automated quality. Own our security PR reviews, automated scans, fixes, and triage.

  • Write it down. Document how we do security so the rest of the team can answer customer questions with confidence.

  • Security habits. Help the engineering team build secure habits with reviews, docs, and light guardrails.

Like everyone at Trigger.dev, you’ll also help in our Discord and GitHub community, write docs, and create content like blog posts, code examples, and videos.

What we’re looking for

  • Senior backend engineer. You design and ship production backend systems yourself.

  • AppSec experience. You’ve done hands-on application security work, such as secure code review, threat modelling, pen testing, CTFs or bug bounties. You don’t need a security job title or to have run a security team.

  • Cloud operations. You’ve run production systems in the cloud.

  • Multi-tenant systems. You’ve built or secured systems where many customers share the same infrastructure.

  • TypeScript. You’re comfortable working in it. Our codebase also uses Go and Rust.

  • AI-forward. You use AI tools to automate testing, detection, and defense.

  • Startup pace. You’ve worked somewhere a step or two ahead of where we are, so you know what good looks like at our size.

  • Owner’s mindset. You take work off the team’s plate and fix what you find.

  • On call. Reliability and security response are shared across the team.

  • In-person time. You’re open to team events a few times a year.

You’ll stand out if you have

  • Built or hardened sandboxes: containers, microVMs, gVisor, Firecracker, WASM, or similar.

  • Secured platforms where customers have their own customers.

  • A track record in bug bounties or CTFs.

  • Contributed to open source.

  • Worked at a developer tools, infrastructure, or open source company.

  • Experience with Go or Rust.

Benefits

  • Compensation and equity. Generous, transparent pay, plus equity so everyone shares in the company’s success.

  • Async working. Need a heads-down day or a meeting-free day? No problem.

  • Home office. We help with equipment so you’re as productive at home as in the office.

  • Vacation. 25 days plus national holidays, sick leave, and generous parental leave.

  • Training budget. An annual budget for books, courses, or an Audible subscription.

  • Pension. Join our company scheme, or we’ll pay into your private pension.

Our values

  • We’re proud to be open source. We believe in the open source community and in building a great free-to-use product.

  • We ship uncomfortably fast. Moving fast is key for a startup. We’re pragmatic about what we build and when.

  • We work autonomously. We decide as a team what will help our customers most, and prioritize from there.

Threat Research Engineer, Security Factory: Threat Research

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Threat Research Engineer, you’ll take ideas from the first question to a working proof of concept, deploy it, and analyze the results yourself. This is a full-stack role, with AI central to how we work. You’ll build agentic workflows for research, analysis, and detection, and use AI tools every day to move faster.

What you’ll do

  • Research new attack surfaces and threat vectors, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems.
  • Find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in open source projects and developer tools.
  • Analyze software supply chain incidents and events.
  • Build AI-powered workflows and agents that automate research, analysis, and detection.
  • Build and maintain the cloud-based systems behind our detection and advisory work.
  • Improve the quality and coverage of our vulnerability and malware advisories.
  • Write up your findings as blog posts and present them at conferences.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

  • Hands-on security experience in research, malware analysis, penetration testing, or security tooling, with both a developer mindset and an adversarial mindset: you can build systems and think about how to break them.
  • Demonstrated experience using AI in real work, such as building with large language model APIs or agent frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or agent SDKs.
  • Strong programming skills in Go or Python, with good software engineering practices including testing, code review, continuous integration and continuous delivery, and maintainable code.
  • Experience deploying and running production services on a public cloud.
  • Understanding of how package ecosystems work and how software supply chain attacks happen.
  • Ability to map possible attack vectors, name trade-offs, and make data-driven decisions, balancing quality and speed with customer outcomes in mind while keeping up with security and AI industry trends.
  • Clear writing that explains findings to both engineers and a general audience.
  • Helpful, but not required: published vulnerability findings; security research on AI agents, large language model applications, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers; Google Cloud Platform experience; or infrastructure as code experience with Terraform or OpenTofu.

You don’t need deep knowledge of compilers or static application security testing engines. A high-level understanding is enough.

About the team

The Threat Research group researches security threats as they emerge and turns what we learn into protection for GitLab customers. We maintain the GitLab Advisory Database, which powers GitLab’s dependency scanning. We also build detection capabilities, do original vulnerability research, and publish what we find. Recent work includes the Shai-Hulud npm worm and a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Serena, a popular MCP coding agent. You can read more on the Security Labs blog.
